name: Kulfa
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

tone_statements.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2009. Entre lac Albert et lac Tchad : l'expansion sara-bongo-baguirmienne. In Henry Tourneux & Noe Woin (eds.), Migrations et mobilite dans le bassin du lac Tchad. Actes du XIIIe colloque international du Reseau Mega-Tchad (Maroua, 31 oct.-3 nov. 2005), 239-252. Marseille: IRD Editions (Colloques et seminaires). HAL halshs-00348136.
tone_statements.quote: Dans le cas particulier des langues SBB, deux domaines sont révélateurs d'innovations partagées : les systèmes tonals et le lexique. Le passage de deux à trois hauteurs tonales distinctives (et les correspondances qui en résultent dans le domaine de la morphologie verbale) caractérise notamment la branche des langues 'occidentales' (*OCC), qui s'est solidairement détachée des autres langues avant de se diversifier à son tour. [...] L'important sous-groupe des langues 'sara' justifie à lui seul l'identification d'un système tardif *SARA dont ces dernières sont issues. [Tableau 3: *OCC > *SARA: ndoka, wad, bagiro, na, tiye, kulfa, sime, dem, bulala, beraku, kenga, barma, sar, mbay, ngambay, bedjond, kaba P.]
tone_statements.translation: In the particular case of the SBB languages, two domains reveal shared innovations: the tone systems and the lexicon. The passage from two to three distinctive tone heights (and the resulting correspondences in verbal morphology) characterises in particular the branch of 'western' languages (*OCC), which split off from the other languages as a block before diversifying in turn. [...] The large subgroup of 'Sara' languages by itself justifies identifying a later system *SARA from which they derive. [Table 3 lists kulfa under *SARA within *OCC.]
tone_statements.locator: HAL author version p. 2, section following Tableau 1 discussion; Tableau 3 'Genealogie des langues SBB (identites tonales et lexique)' p. 9
tone_statements.n_tones: 3 tone heights (branch-level statement for *OCC/*SARA, which includes kulfa)

tone_statements.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal & Pierre Nougayrol. 2004. Les marques personnelles des langues SBB : traits systematiques et perspectives historiques. In Dymitr Ibriszimow & Guillaume Segerer (eds.), Systemes de marques personnelles en Afrique (Afrique et Langage 8), 23-42. Louvain-Paris: Peeters. HAL halshs-00331347.
tone_statements.quote: Les langues occidentales partagent plusieurs innovations systématiques dont la plus significative est l'expansion du registre tonal de deux à trois hauteurs distinctives. Ces modifications justifient que l'on distingue au moins deux types de systèmes historiques communs chronologiquement ordonnés, un système *SBB, valant pour l'ensemble des langues SBB, et un système *OCC, valant pour l'ensemble des seules langues occidentales.
tone_statements.translation: The western languages share several systematic innovations, the most significant of which is the expansion of the tonal register from two to three distinctive heights. These changes justify distinguishing at least two chronologically ordered common historical systems, a *SBB system valid for all SBB languages and an *OCC system valid for the western languages only.
tone_statements.locator: HAL author version section 3 'Du systeme reconstruit aux systemes actuels', p. 4; Schema genealogique p. 13

sources.citation: Keegan, John M. & Koutou Koyombo Prosper. [2014]. Dictionary of Sara Kaba Na (with English introduction). Cuenca: Morkeg Books. 332 pp. [closest described relative; Keegan 2015 p. v: Kulfa phonology 'very similar to that of Sara Kaba Na']
sources.note: Nothing on stress; tone-based description (checked as a proxy only; not Kulfa).

sources.citation: Keegan, John M., Nanga Jean Tadio & Ndoko Masa Singa. 2015. Kulfa Lexicon: Kulfa-French, French-Kulfa. 1st ed. (Oct. 2015). Cuenca: Morkeg Books (Sara-Bagirmi Language Project). 109 pp. [supersedes Tadio & Keegan 2014 Petit Lexique Kulfa / Kulfa Word List listed by Glottolog]
sources.note: Nothing. Front matter (pp. i-x): Alphabet with segment values, 1.1 Phonemes, 1.2 inflection described entirely in terms of three level tones (verb tone classes High-Low/Low-Low, Mid-Mid/Low-Mid, High-Mid), 1.3 auxiliaries; tone marked on every entry. The words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur except 'northern/southern accent' (= dialect).
